pr.title: Open a version-only release pull request by hand, and tag and publish it when it merges
pr.head: 0d63588731afdebed516805b529026122b4d5b8b

summary: trip has no releases yet, and the installer from the layer below installs whatever the v0 tag names. This layer adds what makes those tags. It is the third step of the releases plan, ported from Projector's release process.

You start a release by hand with gh workflow run release.yml -f bump=minor. The workflow opens a pull request that changes only the version. Merging that pull request is the decision to ship: a second job tags the merge commit vX.Y.Z, creates the GitHub release, and then moves v0 to it.

1. Propose. Run from main only, it raises the version in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, commits Release X.Y.Z on release/vX.Y.Z, and refuses that commit if it changes anything else. It then pushes the branch, opens or reuses the pull request, and dispatches the Check workflow onto it, because GitHub starts no workflow for a pull request a workflow's own token opened.
  2. Publish. It runs on each push to main that changes Cargo.toml. It does only the steps the remote lacks, in order: the immutable version tag, the GitHub release, and then v0. A push that leaves the version alone releases nothing.

The review found one open problem. The publish gate compares the old and new versions only for equality, so a push that lowers the version, such as a revert of the first release pull request, still tags, publishes, and moves v0 back.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Release pull request: the pull request the propose job opens on release/vX.Y.Z, changing only the two version files.
  • Version tag: the annotated tag vX.Y.Z. It never moves once pushed.
  • Major tag: v0, which the installer serves. It moves to each new release, last.
  • --since: the previous head of main, the push's before commit, which the publish job compares versions against.

cards.title: Before the first release
cards.html:
• Turn on Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests under Settings > Actions > General. It is off today.
  • The live main ruleset needs no approving review and no status check, so the propose job posts no review status of its own, unlike Projector's.

groups.title: The release script
groups.kicker: Bumping the version, checking the release commit, and publishing a release idempotently
intro: .github/scripts/release.py does every step the workflow needs, so each step can be tested without GitHub. It has four subcommands: bump and set write a new version, check-commit refuses a release commit that changes anything but the version, and tag publishes.

The version is changed as text but read as TOML. A regular expression rewrites only the version line of Cargo.toml's [package] table and the line after name = "trip" in Cargo.lock. tomllib then checks that both files agree, and that the lock has exactly one trip entry. check-commit reuses the same rewrite: a release commit passes only when each file after it equals the file before it with the new version written in.

tag reads which tags the remote already has with git ls-remote, and does only the missing steps, so re-running a failed job finishes the release. With --commit it releases that commit, which must be on origin/main. With --since it returns early when the two commits name the same version.

files.note: New. The version rewrite, the release-commit check, and the publish steps with v0 moved last.

checks.text: Open review finding (P2). The gate skips the release only when the versions are equal, so a push that lowers the version goes through. A revert of the first release pull request tags the revert commit with the never-released version, publishes it, and moves v0 back to it. The fix is to release only when the version rises.

The version tag is created with a local --force, but pushed without one, so an existing remote version tag is never replaced. The rerun test checks that the v0.5.1 tag object is unchanged after a failed release is finished.

check-commit compares each file after the commit with the file before it plus the new version, so a commit that also adds a dependency to Cargo.toml is refused, not only one that touches a third file. A test covers each case.
Every gh call takes its arguments as a list, with no shell, and the only values passed in are the tag name and the repository slug, so nothing here can inject a shell command.

groups.title: The Release workflow
groups.kicker: The propose and publish jobs, and the Check step that runs the script's tests
intro: release.yml has two jobs, each chosen by the event that started the run. A manual workflow_dispatch runs propose, and a push to main that changes Cargo.toml runs publish. The workflow has no pull_request_target or workflow_run trigger. So no pull request, from a fork or otherwise, runs it, and only a merge to main can publish.

The workflow's default token is read-only. propose raises it to write contents, pull requests, and actions, the last so that it can dispatch Check. publish gets contents: write only, for the tag pushes and the release. The two inputs the jobs read, the bump choice and the push's before commit, reach the scripts through env, not through ${{ }} inside run:. Both jobs share one release concurrency group that never cancels a running job.

files.note: New. The propose job opens the release pull request, and the publish job runs release.py tag on the merge commit.

checks.text: A dispatch from another ref is refused, because the release branch would carry that ref's unreviewed commits, and check-commit reads only the release commit.
Check is dispatched onto the release branch, so its results land on the branch's commit, which is the pull request's head.

files.note: Runs python3 tests/release_test.py as its own step after cargo fmt --check, since it needs no trip build.

groups.title: Tests of the release script
groups.kicker: Twenty hermetic cases against a local bare remote and a fake gh
intro: tests/release_test.py drives release.py in temporary directories. The publish cases use a temporary bare repository as the remote and a fake gh on PATH that records its calls and plays GitHub's releases. They push to a branch named trunk, not main, so a developer's pre-push hook does not refuse them. Nothing reaches the network.

files.note: New. Covers the bump, the release-commit check, and each publish path, including finishing a release that failed after its tag was pushed.

checks.text: The review ran it at this patch: Ran 20 tests, OK, in about 7.5 seconds.

groups.title: README and plan
groups.kicker: How to cut a release, and what implementation settled
intro: The README gains a short Releasing section. In the plan, § 2.1 now records the live ruleset, which needs no approving review, and § 9 records the decisions this layer made: no review status, the --since gate, tagging the commit the push made, and checking what the release commit changes, not only which files.

files.note: Adds the Releasing section: the dispatch command, what merging does, and the repository setting the workflow needs.
§ 2.1's ruleset paragraph, and six new § 9 entries. § 2.1 step 4 still says you approve the release pull request, which the paragraph below now says is not required.
